place: Estádio Morenão, Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul
shape: Unidentified lights
witnesses: More than 24,000 spectators, players and the referee
summary: During a Brazilian championship match between Operário and Vasco da Gama, a crowd of more than 24,000 saw unidentified objects over the stadium. Players, including Cocada, and referee José de Assis Aragão described them. Among the spectators was Ademar José Gevaerd, who went on to become one of Brazil's best-known UFO researchers.

title: Hessdalen lights
explanation: Studied since 1983 by Project Hessdalen with an automated measurement station; hypotheses include combustion of dust from the valley’s ores, plasma, and piezoelectric effects.
shape: White, yellow or red floating lights
witnesses: Residents and scientists
summary: Lights have appeared over the 12-km Hessdalen valley since at least the early 1980s, peaking at up to 20 per week in 1981–84. Unusually, they have been measured: radar, spectra, magnetometers and a permanent camera station have recorded them, but their cause is still debated.

title: Hudson Valley "Westchester boomerang"
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: State police and the New York Power Authority attributed the sightings to pilots flying Cessna 152s in tight formation from Stormville Airport with coloured lights — a hoax the pilots reportedly enjoyed.
shape: V / boomerang of coloured lights
witnesses: Thousands across Westchester, Putnam, Dutchess and Fairfield counties
summary: For over a year residents of the Hudson Valley reported a silent boomerang or V of bright lights, sometimes "the size of a football field". Guards at the Indian Point nuclear plant reportedly saw it in June and July 1984, and a Brewster resident videotaped the lights on 24 July.

title: Aeroflot Tu-134 over Minsk — the light that became a cloud
place: Over Minsk, Byelorussian SSR, on the flight to Tallinn
explanation: Western analysts tied it to a Soviet missile launch that night, whose rising plume and glowing exhaust cloud look much like the crew’s sketches: Jonathan McDowell’s launch catalogue lists a submarine-launched R-29R test on September 7, 1984, with a note (after James Oberg) naming it as the source of the sighting. The Soviet army newspaper Krasnaya Zvezda suggested light refracted by floating space debris.
shape: A yellow light that threw out rays, became concentric circles and then a green cloud
witnesses: Captain Igor Cherkashin and co-pilot Gennady Lazurin of an Aeroflot Tu-134, and the crew of a second airliner
duration: Several minutes; the cloud is said to have stayed with the aircraft for hundreds of kilometres
summary: At about 4 a.m. on September 7, 1984, the crew of an Aeroflot Tu-134 flying from Tbilisi via Rostov to Tallinn saw a bright yellow light appear to their right over Byelorussia. It threw out beams strong enough, by one account, to light up the houses and roads below, changed into concentric circles and then into a glowing green cloud that seemed to follow the airliner. Co-pilot Gennady Lazurin sketched it, and Captain Igor Cherkashin called air traffic control, which reported a “double” return on radar; a second airliner flying the opposite way also saw it. The newspaper Trud published the story in early 1985, a rare UFO report in the Soviet press. Rumours that crew members of the second aircraft later died of illnesses caused by the encounter have never been substantiated. Western analysts matched the sketches to the plume of a missile launched that night.

title: Dalnegorsk “Height 611” crash
explanation: Ball lightning and other plasma phenomena have been proposed. The reports of unusual metal fragments come mostly from the investigating group and have not been independently confirmed.
shape: Reddish sphere about 3 m across
witnesses: Residents of Dalnegorsk
summary: On the evening of January 29, 1986 residents of the mining town of Dalnegorsk saw a reddish, silent sphere about three metres across flying from the south-east at some 700–800 metres, at about 15 m/s. It crossed part of the town and came down on Izvestkovaya mountain, known as Height 611, burning on the slope. Investigators reported tiny metallic droplets 2–5 mm across, and fibres in a tangle of metal, quartz and gold-coloured threads. In Russia it is often called the best-documented UFO crash, although the technical findings come mainly from the group that investigated it.

title: Brazil’s "Official UFO Night"
place: São José dos Campos – Rio de Janeiro – Goiás
explanation: The Air Force commander said "we have no explanation". The report declassified in 2009 described objects with speeds from hovering to supersonic and 90° turns.
shape: Red, white and green lights; 21 radar plots
witnesses: Controllers, F-5E and Mirage pilots, Embraer founder Ozires Silva
summary: Controllers at São José dos Campos and radar across south-east Brazil tracked about 21 unknown contacts. Embraer’s founder, flying in, saw red lights; the Air Force scrambled F-5Es from Santa Cruz and Mirage IIIs from Anápolis. Pilots reported lights that kept their distance and targets that appeared behind them.

title: Torpo film
shape: Two bright objects, one flashing and throwing sparks
witnesses: A family and friends at a mountain farm
summary: A couple at a mountain farm near Torpo, with their son and friends, watched two bright objects in the evening sky, one moving dramatically, flashing and throwing off sparks. The husband filmed them. Ground Saucer Watch found no sign of a hoax, but said the apparent motion could come from camera shake and that the lack of reference points made the film inconclusive.

title: Japan Air Lines Flight 1628
explanation: The FAA’s radar returns were later dismissed as clutter / a split image; Philip Klass argued the crew saw Jupiter and Mars. The FAA found the crew professional and rational.
shape: Two small lights and a huge "mothership"
witnesses: Capt. Kenji Terauchi and crew
summary: A JAL Boeing 747 freighter on the Reykjavík–Anchorage leg reported three objects pacing it at 35,000 ft, including one Terauchi described as enormous. Anchorage controllers reported returns near the aircraft; the objects stayed with the plane through turns and descents until near Talkeetna.

title: Gulf Breeze photographs
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: Considered a hoax. In 1990 the new owners of Ed Walters's former house found a styrofoam model UFO in the attic that a reporter used to reproduce the photos almost exactly. A local teenager also said he had helped fake them. Walters said the model was planted.
shape: Cylindrical craft with a ring of portholes and a glowing base
witnesses: Ed Walters; other residents later came forward
summary: Contractor Ed Walters gave the Gulf Breeze Sentinel five Polaroids of a glowing craft he said hovered near his home. Over six months he produced dozens more photos and video, and described being hit by a blue beam and seeing aliens. Researchers such as Bruce Maccabee backed the photos, and other residents reported sightings. After the model was found in 1990 and a reporter recreated the pictures, the case became a textbook example of a UFO photo hoax.

title: Ilkley Moor photograph
explanation: Critics say the blurry photograph could show a person or a cardboard cutout, and ask why no picture of the craft was taken. Kodak experts found no sign of tampering, but the image is too grainy for firm conclusions, and the account changed under hypnosis.
shape: Small green humanoid; two-part silver craft
witnesses: Philip Spencer, a retired police officer (a pseudonym)
duration: Minutes; about two hours unaccounted for
summary: On the morning of December 1, 1987 Philip Spencer, a retired police officer, was walking across Ilkley Moor, between Ilkley and Keighley, when he said he met a small dark-green figure about 1.2 metres tall, with a large head and long thin arms. He took one photograph before it ran off, then saw a whitish, two-part craft rise from the moor with a loud hum. About two hours were missing from his journey, and his compass pointed the wrong way. A wildlife photographer said the figure matched no known animal and Kodak found no signs of tampering, but the US Navy optics specialist Bruce Maccabee called the image too grainy to test. Under hypnosis in March 1988 his story changed to one of being taken aboard and examined.

title: Knowles family encounter
place: Nullarbor Plain, between Madura and Mundrabilla, Western Australia
explanation: No explanation has been established. The account rests on the four family members’ testimony and the physical details they described, and has been widely reported in Australia.
shape: Large glowing ball
witnesses: Faye Knowles and her sons Patrick, Sean and Wayne
summary: In the early hours of January 20, 1988, the Knowles family were driving across the Nullarbor Plain in their station wagon when a bright light appeared ahead. They said a large glowing object pursued the car for a long time and finally came down on the roof; the car seemed to be lifted off the road, and the engine and voices changed as if time were slowing. Mrs Knowles said she reached out of the rear window, felt something soft and warm on the roof, and found her hand covered in black dust. When the car dropped back onto the road a rear tyre burst. The family reported it at Mundrabilla. It is one of Australia’s best-known close-encounter stories.

title: Villa Urquiza Christmas sighting
shape: Silver object
witnesses: More than 7,500
summary: On Christmas Day 1988 a silver object crossed the Villa Urquiza neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, watched by thousands of people. The city airport reported an object heading west toward Avenida General Paz. It is often called Argentina's most spectacular UFO sighting.

title: Kapustin Yar — the KGB file on a night of lights over a missile depot
place: Military sites 30–45 km from Kapustin Yar, Astrakhan oblast
explanation: The reports are in a package of 124 pages that the KGB sent to the cosmonaut Pavel Popovich in October 1991, with a covering letter saying that the KGB did not study UFO reports but passed on what it received. No investigation or conclusion accompanies them, and the original file was later said to have gone missing.
shape: A disc 4–5 m across with a dome, glowing dim green, with a bright flashing light and a beam
witnesses: Officers and soldiers of military units near Kapustin Yar, among them Ensign V. N. Voloshin, Capt. Chernikov and Sr Lt Klimenko
duration: About three and a half hours
summary: Between 22:10 on July 28 and 01:30 on July 29, 1989, soldiers and officers at military sites 30 to 45 km from the Kapustin Yar missile range, described in the reports as a transmission centre and a rocket-weapons depot, reported unidentified objects. At the depot, Ensign Valery Voloshin and a private watched through binoculars for about two hours as a disc some 4–5 m across with a dome, glowing a dim phosphorescent green, hovered 20 to 70 m above the warehouses, flashed a bright light and swept a beam, moved silently in sudden jerks, and finally left towards Akhtubinsk. Other officers described flashes like electric welding, a “flying plate” or a cigar-shaped object, and an aircraft was said to have been sent up but kept at a distance. The written statements, with unit names blacked out, were among 124 pages of military and civilian reports that the KGB passed in October 1991 to Pavel Popovich, president of a Soviet ufological association; Komsomolskaya Pravda published them in 2003. They are first-hand military reports, but nothing shows that anyone examined them.

title: Voronezh park landing
explanation: Reported by the Soviet news agency TASS; later widely regarded as a children’s story amplified by the press.
shape: Large red sphere / oval
witnesses: Mainly children in a city park
summary: TASS reported that children in a Voronezh park saw a large red ball land and tall beings emerge. Soviet reporting of the case — unusual at the time — made headlines worldwide.

title: Pereslavl-Zalessky — the Soviet air defence report
shape: A disc 100–200 m across with two pulsing lights on its sides
witnesses: More than 100 observers reported by air-defence units of the Moscow Military District; interceptor pilots Lt Col A. A. Semenchenko and others; radar crews
summary: On the night of March 21, 1990, air-defence units of the Moscow Military District reported more than 100 visual sightings of an object near Pereslavl-Zalessky. At 21:38 Lt Col A. A. Semenchenko was scrambled to identify a target at about 2,000 m; he saw two flashing white lights and a dim silhouette against the lights of the town, and the target did not answer his identification interrogation. Other pilots and radar posts gave times, bearings and distances; one ground radar post reported a fast-moving shining object with red lights, followed by another with white lights. In Rabochaya Tribuna on April 19, Colonel General Igor Maltsev, chief of the Main Staff of the Soviet Air Defence Forces, published excerpts: a disc 100 to 200 m across with two pulsing lights, flying silently between 1,000 and 7,000 m, at two to three times the speed of a modern fighter, rotating and hovering. Maltsev said he was “not a specialist on UFOs” and could only correlate the data. It was the first time a Soviet commander of that rank described such a case in public; the underlying reports have not been released, and no explanation was published.

title: Belgian UFO wave — F-16 intercepts
explanation: The Belgian Air Force report left the radar contacts unexplained; critics attribute the F-16 lock-ons to the other fighter and to Bragg scattering. The famous Petit-Rechain triangle photo was admitted to be a hoax in 2011.
shape: Dark triangle with bright corner lights
witnesses: ~13,500 reports in the wave; gendarmes; Air Force
summary: Beginning with a sighting by two gendarmes at Eupen on 29 November 1989, thousands of Belgians reported large, slow triangles with lights. On the night of 30–31 March 1990, after ground and radar reports, two Belgian Air Force F-16s from Beauvechain made nine interception attempts and obtained brief radar locks; the Air Force published its report openly.

title: Calvine photograph
explanation: The MoD never explained it; proposed explanations include a rock reflected in water and a hoax. The photographers have never been identified.
shape: Large diamond hovering; a Harrier jet nearby
witnesses: Two unidentified walkers
summary: Two men walking above Calvine photographed a large, silent diamond-shaped object hovering while a military jet flew past. Their negatives went from the Daily Record to the Ministry of Defence and vanished. A surviving print surfaced in 2022 and was published worldwide.

title: The “immense triangle” over France — a Proton re-entry
place: From the Bay of Biscay across France to Alsace
explanation: The re-entry of the third stage of the Soviet Proton rocket that launched Gorizont 21 (catalogue object 20925, 1990-094C), identified by NASA on November 8 and confirmed by CNES orbit specialists; GEIPAN classes the case A, fully explained.
shape: Three main lights in a group, read by many as an immense luminous triangle, with sparks and smoke trailing
witnesses: Thousands, including CNES astronaut Jean-Pierre Haigneré and balloon technicians at Aire-sur-Adour
summary: At about 7 p.m. on November 5, 1990, a slow procession of bright lights crossed France from the Bay of Biscay to Alsace. Gendarmerie stations were flooded with calls, and for more than a week SEPRA, the CNES unit then in charge, answered witnesses describing “an immense luminous triangle”; the astronaut Jean-Pierre Haigneré was among them, and technicians at the CNES balloon base at Aire-sur-Adour held a launch to watch. On November 8 NASA identified the re-entry of object 20925, the third stage of the Proton rocket that had put the Gorizont 21 satellite into orbit, and CNES confirmed its track across France. The case, which fell in the middle of the Belgian wave, is a standard example of how a known re-entry is reported as a structured craft.

title: Montreal — lights over the Bonaventure Hotel
shape: Ring of 8–10 bright lights; a huge round form
witnesses: Hotel guests and staff, passers-by, police officers
summary: From 7:20 to 10:20 p.m., people on the rooftop pool deck of the Bonaventure Hotel and in the streets below watched 8 to 10 lights hanging in a circle above them, sending down bright white rays. Some described a huge round object behind the lights. Police officers attended, and the next day La Presse reported the sighting. It drifted slowly north and was never identified.

title: Alitalia MD-80 near miss over Kent
explanation: The Civil Aviation Authority and the Ministry of Defence looked at missiles, weather balloons and rockets and ruled each one out, then closed the inquiry without an answer. The files were released by the National Archives in October 2008.
shape: Brown, missile-shaped object
witnesses: Capt. Achille Zaghetti, with 57 people aboard
summary: At about 8 p.m. on April 21, 1991, an Alitalia MD-80 flying from Milan to Heathrow with 57 people aboard was at 22,000 feet over the army ranges at Lydd, on the Kent coast, when Capt. Achille Zaghetti saw a brown, missile-shaped object pass about 1,000 feet above the airliner and shouted “Look out, look out”. The London control centre told him it had an unknown target on radar 10 nautical miles behind him. The Ministry of Defence and the Civil Aviation Authority investigated as an airmiss, ruled out a missile, a weather balloon and a rocket, and closed the case unsolved.

title: Mexico City eclipse videos
explanation: Astronomers identified the brightest object as Venus (with Mars and Regulus nearby), made visible by the darkness of totality. Reflections in glass, camera artefacts and hoaxes account for others; not every video has been explained.
shape: Metallic disc or bright point, sometimes with a wavy haze
witnesses: Dozens of video and photo recordings by different people
summary: Millions in Mexico watched the total solar eclipse of July 11, 1991, with totality in Mexico City at 13:24 and lasting more than six minutes. At least 16 photographers and videographers recorded a bright, disc-like object near the Sun in the sky, some with a wavy trail of haze behind it. The sightings were widely seen on television and the case is a classic in Mexican ufology. Astronomers pointed out that the darkness of totality shows Venus, which stood a few degrees from the star Regulus, and that other planets also come into view, which fits many of the videos but not necessarily the apparent motion some of them show.

title: Crop circles — Doug Bower and Dave Chorley own up
place: The fields of Hampshire and Wiltshire; their first circles near Cheesefoot Head, Winchester
explanation: Made by people. Doug Bower and Dave Chorley showed how they had made circles since 1978 with a plank, rope and a cap with a wire sighting loop, made one for journalists that a leading “cerealogist” declared genuine, and inspired the teams who make the elaborate designs today.
shape: Circles of flattened cereal crop, later rings and complex patterns
witnesses: Doug Bower and Dave Chorley, and the journalists they demonstrated to
summary: From the late 1970s, circles of flattened wheat and barley appeared each summer in the fields of southern England, especially Hampshire and Wiltshire. By the late 1980s they were a national story, explained as UFO landing marks (“saucer nests”), as plasma vortices by the meteorologist Terence Meaden, and as messages by a new class of “cerealogists”. In September 1991 two men from Southampton, Doug Bower and Dave Chorley, told the newspaper Today that they had made circles since 1978, inspired by the 1966 Tully “saucer nest” in Australia, starting near Cheesefoot Head, and claimed more than 200 of them. They showed their tools, a plank, a rope and a cap with a wire loop to keep a straight line, and made a circle for journalists that the cerealogist Pat Delgado then declared authentic. Not every circle since is theirs, but none has been shown to have any cause other than people.

title: Cosford incident
place: RAF Cosford and RAF Shawbury, Shropshire
explanation: Most of the evening reports matched the re-entry of the rocket body that had launched the Russian satellite Cosmos 2238. The MoD found no threat. Nick Pope, who investigated for the MoD, argued that later reports, including a meteorological officer's at RAF Shawbury, were never explained.
shape: Triangular craft; lights in formation
witnesses: Police officers, RAF personnel, members of the public
summary: Over the night of March 30–31, 1993, police officers, RAF personnel and the public across England and Wales reported lights in formation and a large triangular craft. A patrol at RAF Cosford saw it pass over the base. At RAF Shawbury a meteorological officer described a huge craft moving slowly across the airfield and sweeping a light beam over the ground. The MoD's Nick Pope pressed the case internally, and the files were later released to The National Archives.

title: Air France 3532 — radar-visual over Coulommiers
explanation: GEIPAN, the French space agency’s UAP office, classes the case as unexplained after investigation. The military radar track is real but does not match the crew’s account closely: the crew saw a stationary object far off to the left, while the radar target was about a mile to the right and moving. Both vanished at the same moment.
shape: Huge brown or dark-red disc or bell that seemed to change shape
witnesses: Capt. Jean-Charles Duboc, First Officer Valérie Chauffour and a chief steward
summary: At 13:14 on January 28, 1994, the crew of Air France flight 3532, an Airbus A320 from Nice to London, was cruising at about 11,900 metres near Coulommiers, east of Paris, when the chief steward and both pilots saw a huge object, like a brown bell or disc, off to the left. It seemed to change shape, stayed in view for about a minute and then vanished abruptly. Reims air traffic control had no traffic there, but the military radar at Cinq-Mars-la-Pile recorded a track for about 50 seconds that crossed the airliner’s path and disappeared at the same moment the crew lost sight of the object. The radar return and the crew’s description do not agree on distance or side, which is part of why the case remains open.

title: Lake Michigan lights — 911 calls and a weather radar
place: The Lake Michigan shore of Ottawa and Muskegon counties, Michigan (Grand Haven to Holland)
shape: Five or six round or cylindrical objects with red, green, blue and white lights, like flickering Christmas lights
witnesses: Dozens of residents who called 911, police officers, and the meteorologist on duty at the Muskegon weather office
summary: On the night of March 8, 1994, dozens of people along the Lake Michigan shore of western Michigan called 911 about lights over the lake: five or six objects with red, green, blue and white lights that hovered and moved erratically. Police officers saw them too. A dispatcher called the National Weather Service office at Muskegon County Airport, and the meteorologist on duty, Jack Bushong, turned the office’s WSR-74C weather radar on the area and saw several returns where none should be, which he said moved fast and changed direction; he reported it to the National UFO Reporting Center. Days later the Weather Service played the radar down, saying it was built to see rain, not aircraft. Over the following weeks more than 300 people in 42 Michigan counties reported sightings; MUFON investigators interviewed dozens and found no explanation. Bushong kept his account for decades, and the case stays one of the better-documented police and radar cases of the 1990s.

title: Ariel School, Ruwa
explanation: Skeptics suggest mass suggestion after a meteor/re-entry seen across southern Africa two days earlier; many former pupils still stand by their accounts.
shape: Silver craft landing in scrub; small beings
witnesses: 62 pupils aged 5–12
summary: During morning break, 62 children said a silver craft landed in bush beside the playground and one or two small figures in black watched them. Their drawings were collected within days, and Harvard psychiatrist John Mack interviewed them.

title: British Airways 5061 near miss over the Pennines
place: About 8 nautical miles south-east of Manchester Airport
explanation: The Civil Aviation Authority’s Joint Airmiss Working Group could not identify the object and rated the airmiss “unassessable”. No other aircraft or balloon was found, and no radar return was seen.
shape: Wedge-shaped object with small white lights and a black stripe
witnesses: Capt. Roger Wills and First Officer Mark Stuart
summary: At 18:48 on January 6, 1995, British Airways flight 5061, a Boeing 737 from Milan with 60 passengers aboard, was descending through about 4,000 feet over the Pennines toward Manchester when both pilots saw a lighted object pass very close down the right side, going the other way. They described it as wedge-shaped, with small white lights and a black stripe; the first officer ducked as it went by. Nothing showed on radar. The Joint Airmiss Working Group studied the report and, unable to identify the object, called it “unassessable”.

title: America West Flight 564 over the Texas Panhandle
place: Over Bovina, Texas, near the New Mexico border
shape: A row of white lights flashing in sequence; a long, dark, cigar-shaped silhouette against lightning
witnesses: The crew of a Boeing 757: the first officer, the captain and a flight attendant; Albuquerque Center controllers
summary: On the night of May 25, 1995, America West Flight 564, a Boeing 757 flying west at 39,000 ft from Tampa to Las Vegas, was passing over Bovina in the Texas Panhandle when the first officer, John Waller, and a flight attendant saw a row of bright white lights off to the right and below, flashing in sequence from left to right. When lightning lit the thunderclouds behind it, the crew saw a dark, wingless, cigar-shaped silhouette, which they estimated at 300 to 400 ft long, though its distance was unknown. Waller asked Albuquerque Center about traffic; the controllers had nothing on their radar and called NORAD, which reported a track that later proved to be a small aircraft with a faulty transponder. The next morning a controller said NORAD had tracked another target that stopped and accelerated repeatedly, but that was never confirmed. Walter Webb investigated for the Fund for UFO Research, interviewed the crew and the controllers and obtained the FAA tapes, and found no explanation; the SETI astronomer Seth Shostak later remarked that bright planets fool trained pilots, without analysing this case.

title: Bariloche — the blackout and Aerolíneas Argentinas 674
place: San Carlos de Bariloche airport, Río Negro, Argentina
explanation: No explanation was found. Carlos Angueira, president of a local astronomy association, rejected a meteorite or a refraction, saying such things cannot “stop in the middle of the sky”. The case drew new attention in 2026, when it appeared among the Latin American incidents in UAP files released by the Pentagon.
shape: A light between white and amber, like a star but much larger; later described as green and white, about 30 m across
witnesses: Capt. Jorge Polanco, his crew and passengers; the tower chief, Daniel García; the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne
summary: At about 8:15 p.m. on July 31, 1995, Aerolíneas Argentinas flight 674, a Boeing 727 from Buenos Aires under Capt. Jorge Polanco, was coming in to land at Bariloche when the airport lost power, and then the whole city went dark as the airliner neared the runway, forcing a go-around. A light “between white and amber”, like a star but much larger and brighter, then flew on a parallel course about 100 metres from the plane. When the power came back the 727 climbed to 3,000 metres, descended and landed, and the light left at full speed toward the south-east. The tower chief and the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne flying 600 metres higher saw it too, and the tower’s instruments swung from one direction to another for no clear reason. Interviewed in 2026, Polanco said: “It pursued us, accompanied us for 17 minutes.”

title: Varginha "ET"
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: A Brazilian Army inquiry concluded that the women had seen a local man with a mental disability, known as "Mudinho", and that the military movements were routine.
shape: Crouching humanoid with red eyes
witnesses: 3 young women; later many rumours
summary: Three young women said they saw a strange creature crouched near a wall, with vein-like marks on its skin, three bumps on its head and eyes like "two red balls". Rumours followed of military trucks carrying captured beings, bodies at hospitals, a police officer's death and animal deaths at the zoo. It became Brazil's best-known UFO story and a local tourist theme.

title: Pretoria police helicopter chase
shape: Bright, colour-changing light
witnesses: About 200 police officers; helicopter crew
summary: At 4 a.m., Sgt Nico Stander of the Adriaan Vlok police station in Pretoria reported lights in the sky, which were videotaped. Some 200 officers and a Bo-105 police helicopter followed them east. The helicopter gave up at about 10,000 ft over the Cullinan area when it ran low on fuel. The lights were seen again on the nights of August 31 and September 1.

title: The Wash incident
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: The radar returns were at least partly explained as echoes from St Botolph's Church ("the Boston Stump"), and the visual sightings as stars and planets.
shape: Rotating, multicoloured light
witnesses: Police officer David Leyland; other witnesses
summary: In the early morning a police officer on the Lincolnshire coast reported a rotating, multicoloured object over The Wash. The Claxby air traffic control radar reported a return in the same area. The report went up through RAF Kinloss and MoD Northwood before the conventional explanation was accepted.

title: Phoenix Lights
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: The ~20:00–20:45 V-formation was traced to A-10 aircraft of Operation Snowbird returning to Davis-Monthan AFB; the ~22:00 row of lights filmed over Phoenix were LUU-2 flares dropped over the Barry Goldwater Range. Some witnesses, including then-governor Fife Symington, reject this.
shape: Huge V / carpenter’s square with five lights
witnesses: Thousands along a 300-mile corridor
summary: A V-shaped formation of lights was reported moving south-east from the Nevada line, over Prescott Valley and Phoenix to Tucson. Later that night a stationary row of amber lights was widely filmed over Phoenix. The event remains one of the most-witnessed UFO events in U.S. history.

title: Howden Moor — sonic booms and the search for a crash
place: Howden Moors, Dark Peak, on the Derbyshire–South Yorkshire border
explanation: The British Geological Survey said the recorded signal was atmospheric, not an impact, and most likely a supersonic aircraft. The MoD admitted a low-flying exercise by six RAF Tornados that it said had ended at 21:30, and denied any supersonic flight; an RAF Police inquiry in 1998 found no military link and suggested a natural cause such as a re-entry. The researcher David Clarke argues that a covert military flight continued after the exercise.
shape: A large low aircraft with lit windows, a dark triangle, two red lights, then an orange glow and smoke
witnesses: A special constable and her husband near Bolsterstone, gamekeepers, farmers, a Peak Park warden and others
summary: Shortly before 10 p.m. on March 24, 1997, people around the moors north-west of Sheffield saw low aircraft and heard explosions. Near Bolsterstone, Special Constable Marie-France Tattersfield and her husband saw a large aircraft with all its windows lit cross in front of them at no more than about 500 ft; a farmer saw a low plane head towards the moor, then an orange glow and plumes of smoke; gamekeepers heard “a terrific explosion”; others described a dark triangle or two red lights. Seismic and acoustic instruments of the British Geological Survey recorded two sonic events, at 21:52 and 22:06. Fearing an air crash, South Yorkshire Police led one of the largest searches in the region’s history: police and RAF helicopters and about 141 mountain-rescue volunteers searched up to 50 square miles of moorland for some 15 hours and found nothing. The Ministry of Defence first said no RAF aircraft was responsible, then admitted that six Tornados had been on low-flying training until 21:30, denied that any had gone supersonic, and closed the case after an RAF Police inquiry with “no military link”. The booms remain unattributed.

title: Southern Illinois police sightings
explanation: The FAA suggested an advertising blimp; the officers’ descriptions of speed and size are hard to reconcile with that.
shape: Huge triangle / "arrowhead" with bright lights
witnesses: 5 police officers in 4 towns, a store owner
summary: Before dawn, a store owner in Highland and then police officers in Lebanon, Summerfield, Shiloh and Dupo independently reported a large, low triangular object with bright lights moving south-west toward Scott AFB and the Mississippi.

title: Mexican Air Force FLIR — Campeche
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: Most analysts identified the lights as gas flares on Cantarell offshore oil platforms seen over the horizon by the infrared camera.
shape: 11 bright infrared lights
witnesses: Mexican Air Force Merlin C-26A crew
summary: A Mexican Air Force surveillance aircraft hunting drug flights recorded 11 bright objects on its infrared camera at about 11,500 ft. The Defence Department released the tape on 12 May 2004.

title: Tinley Park lights
place: Tinley Park and Oak Forest, Illinois
explanation: Commonly attributed to balloons or kites carrying lights or flares, which match the slow drift and the colour. No one has come forward, and the cause has not been confirmed.
shape: Three to four red lights in a triangle
witnesses: Hundreds in the south suburbs of Chicago
summary: On the evening of August 21, 2004, hundreds of people in Chicago's south suburbs watched three large red lights in a triangle drift slowly and silently across the sky. Many filmed them. The lights returned on October 31, 2004 and on several nights in 2005 and 2006, and appeared on national television. They are a prominent "black triangle" style case with plenty of video.

title: USS Nimitz "Tic Tac"
place: Pacific Ocean ~100 mi SW of San Diego
explanation: The Pentagon released the FLIR1 video in 2020 and describes the object as unidentified. Skeptics argue the FLIR clip shows a distant aircraft; the pilots’ visual account is independent of the video.
evidence: video | sensor-data | radar | pilot-witness | military-witness | official-document
shape: White, smooth 40-ft "Tic Tac"
witnesses: 4 aircrew (Fravor, Dietrich + WSOs), USS Princeton radar operators
summary: For days the cruiser USS Princeton’s SPY-1 radar tracked objects appearing at about 80,000 ft, dropping rapidly toward the sea and hovering. On 14 November, Cdr. David Fravor and Lt. Cdr. Alex Dietrich were vectored to a contact and saw a white Tic Tac-shaped object above a churning patch of ocean. It mirrored Fravor’s descent, then accelerated away; seconds later Princeton reported it at the pilots’ CAP point ~60 miles away. A later sortie filmed the FLIR1 video.

title: Río de la Plata — two airliners and a rising light
place: Over the Río de la Plata between Ezeiza (Buenos Aires) and Carrasco (Montevideo)
shape: A luminous object moving upwards
witnesses: The pilot of an Aeromas cargo aircraft, a Lufthansa crew and a Uruguayan military pilot
summary: At about 4 a.m. on Monday, April 4, 2005, the pilot of a Uruguayan Aeromas cargo aircraft that had just left Ezeiza reported a luminous object near his aircraft over the Río de la Plata. The Ezeiza tower suggested it was an engine of a Lufthansa airliner in the area, but the Lufthansa pilot told him he had seen the light too, that it moved upwards and so could not be a meteorite, and called it a missile. A Uruguayan military pilot flying at the same time confirmed a fast luminous object. The reports went through the Carrasco and Ezeiza control towers; the Argentine Air Force recorded the report at Ezeiza, the Argentine armed forces said none of their aircraft or ships were in the area, and the Uruguayan Air Force opened an investigation. No result was published.

title: Chicago O’Hare disc
explanation: The FAA called it a "weather phenomenon" and did not investigate; conditions suited a hole-punch cloud. Nothing appeared on radar.
shape: Dark grey metallic disc, 6–24 ft
witnesses: ~12 United Airlines employees; people outside the airport
summary: A ramp worker pushing back United Flight 446 saw a dark disc hovering low over Gate C-17; pilots, supervisors and mechanics came out to watch. Witnesses said it shot straight up through the overcast, leaving a clear hole in the clouds that closed moments later. The story emerged via a Chicago Tribune FOIA request.

title: Alderney airline sighting
explanation: Jersey radar showed only a faint primary return; proposed explanations include earthquake lights and sun dogs.
shape: Two bright yellow cigar/disc shapes with dark bands
witnesses: Aurigny captain Ray Bowyer, passengers, a second pilot
summary: Flying an Aurigny Trislander from Southampton to Alderney, Capt. Ray Bowyer saw two very large, brilliant yellow objects apparently stationary over the sea, confirmed by passengers and by the pilot of another aircraft. He filed an official report with the Civil Aviation Authority.

title: Stephenville, Texas
explanation: The Air Force said F-16s from the 457th Fighter Squadron were training in the area. A MUFON analysis of FAA radar data claimed an untransponded target heading toward the Crawford ranch; this is not officially confirmed.
shape: Huge, silent, lit object up to a mile long
witnesses: ~40 residents incl. a pilot and a constable
summary: Dozens of people around Stephenville, including a private pilot and a local constable, reported a very large, silent object with bright lights followed by fighter jets. FOIA radar records later analysed by MUFON showed unidentified returns in the area.

title: Cláudio — Military Police report
shape: Luminous figures; lights in the sky
witnesses: 7 Military Police officers and residents
summary: Over the night of November 19–20, 2008, officers of the Minas Gerais Military Police said they chased luminous humanoid figures and photographed lights in the sky around the town of Cláudio. Seven officers signed the report, which includes three photographs and a police incident record.

title: Morristown lights (admitted hoax)
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: Hoax. Joe Rudy and Chris Russo tied road flares to helium balloons and released them on five nights, then revealed it on April 1, 2009 with video of the launches. They were fined for disorderly conduct.
shape: Five red lights in a line and arc
witnesses: Dozens of residents, police, Morristown Airport tower staff
summary: Around 8:15 p.m. on January 5, 2009, residents of Hanover Township, Morristown and nearby towns saw five red lights hanging in the sky and called 9-1-1. Tower staff at Morristown Airport also saw them, but radar showed nothing. TV news and UFO groups covered the lights, and they returned on four more nights. The two men who launched the balloons had also given TV interviews posing as witnesses. They called it a social experiment to show how unreliable eyewitness claims can be.

title: Norwegian spiral
place: Northern Norway and Sweden (seen from Troms and Finnmark)
explanation: A failed test of a Russian RSM-56 Bulava submarine-launched missile from the White Sea: the third stage malfunctioned, and the spinning missile sprayed fuel in a spiral lit by the Sun. The Russian Defence Ministry confirmed the failure the next day.
shape: Blue beam with an expanding white spiral
witnesses: Thousands across northern Norway and Sweden
summary: Before sunrise on December 9, 2009, people across northern Norway saw a blue-white light rise from behind the mountains, stop, and begin to spin. A glowing spiral grew outward and dissolved into a black hole-like disc. Photos and video went worldwide within hours. Astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell quickly suggested a failed Russian missile, and Moscow confirmed a Bulava test failure.

title: Harbour Mille — the “missiles” over Fortune Bay
explanation: Canada and France both said no missile or rocket had been launched; France’s M51 test from the submarine Le Terrible was on a different day and did not match the time or direction. A Royal Military College engineer judged the object subsonic and much smaller than a missile; federal officials suggested model rockets, which the witnesses rejected; and a television station later aired viewer video from the same time that showed a passing aircraft, whose contrail lit by the setting sun would look like a fiery trail. The RCMP closed the file as an unexplained sighting.
shape: Three large grey or silver “bullets” with fire behind them and trails of smoke
witnesses: Emmy Pardy, the postmaster, and two neighbours, one of whom, Darlene Stewart, took photographs
summary: At about sunset on Monday, January 25, 2010, Emmy Pardy and two friends in the small community of Harbour Mille, on Newfoundland’s south coast, saw three objects moving fast across the sky over Fortune Bay. Through binoculars Pardy described one as large and grey or silver with fire coming out of it; they trailed smoke. Darlene Stewart, who had been photographing the sunset, took pictures. When the photographs reached the news, the story became a small political puzzle: the RCMP first spoke of a missile launch and withdrew it, the Prime Minister’s Office said no rocket had been launched, the Defence Minister called the information “spotty”, and the French embassy said there had been no French military activity near Newfoundland or Saint-Pierre and Miquelon.

title: The spiral over eastern Australia — Falcon 9’s first flight
place: Eastern Australia: New South Wales, the Australian Capital Territory and Queensland
explanation: The second stage of the first SpaceX Falcon 9, launched from Cape Canaveral at 18:45 UTC on June 4 with a test Dragon capsule, passed over eastern Australia about an hour later. The stage was rolling, and propellant or gas leaking from it formed a lit spiral, as the Bulava missile’s did over Norway six months earlier. Satellite observers matched the time and the ground track; Sydney Observatory also said it was the rocket.
shape: A large white light with a spiral, “lollipop-type swirl”
witnesses: Dozens of people who sent photographs and videos to ABC News, among many others
summary: Before dawn on Saturday, June 5, 2010, people across New South Wales, the ACT and Queensland saw a large white light with a spiral around it, which seemed to hover briefly and then drift east out of sight. ABC News received dozens of photographs and videos. Astronomers first suggested space junk, a satellite or a rocket, and Sydney Observatory’s Geoffrey Wyatt suggested a rocket spun for stability. The answer came within a day: the Falcon 9 rocket, flying for the first time, had lifted off from Florida at 2:45 p.m. EDT on June 4 (4:45 a.m. in Sydney), and its second stage, with the Dragon qualification unit attached, was due over eastern Australia between about 5:30 and 5:45 a.m. The second stage had been rotating unexpectedly during the flight.

title: Hangzhou Xiaoshan Airport closure
explanation: Chinese UFO research groups found no radar images and concluded the object was probably an aircraft, possibly military.
shape: Bright object over the airport
witnesses: Airport staff and pilots
summary: A bright unidentified object above the airport led authorities to close Xiaoshan and divert flights for about an hour.

title: Montevideo — the photo from the national team’s homecoming
place: Palacio Legislativo and Avenida del Libertador, Montevideo
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: The Uruguayan Air Force’s commission CRIDOVNI found the photographs genuine but rated a conventional cause 97% likely: a light object such as nylon, paper or cloth carried up by rising air over the avenue, with no one having seen anything at the time.
shape: A semicircular object in the sky
witnesses: Fans who photographed the celebration; no direct witness of the object came forward
summary: On July 13, 2010, huge crowds met Uruguay’s football team at the Palacio Legislativo in Montevideo after its fourth place at the World Cup. One fan’s photograph, and others taken at the same spot, showed a semicircular object in the sky, and the picture spread as a UFO. The Uruguayan Air Force’s commission for UFO reports, CRIDOVNI, examined it and reported on July 28: it put the chance of fraud by the photographer or anyone else, and of a psychological effect, at zero, but gave a 97% probability to a conventional object, something like a piece of nylon, paper or cloth lifted by the rising air currents over Avenida del Libertador. No one who had seen the object itself came forward.

title: El Bosque Air Base — the object in the air-show video
explanation: Chile’s aerial-phenomena committee CEFAA said the object could not be explained and estimated a speed of thousands of km/h, which depends entirely on an assumed distance. Independent analysts, among them the HoaxKiller project and the neurologist Steven Novella, showed that the frames match an insect flying close to the camera, which nobody present would have noticed.
shape: A small dark object darting past the jets
witnesses: Spectators at an air show who filmed it; nobody saw the object at the time
duration: A fraction of a second per pass
summary: On the morning of November 5, 2010, the Chilean Air Force held a change-of-command ceremony with an air show at El Bosque Air Base in Santiago, with the Halcones aerobatic team, F-5s and F-16s. An engineer from the nearby aircraft factory, reviewing his own video in slow motion, noticed a small object that seemed to loop near the jets, and handed it to CEFAA, the committee of the civil aviation directorate that studies aerial phenomena. CEFAA gathered seven videos from different spectators and, at a press conference on March 13, 2012, said an astronomer had ruled out a meteoroid, space debris, a bird and an aircraft, estimated the object’s speed at over 6,500 km/h and said the incident could not be explained scientifically. Nobody at the show had noticed anything. Critics pointed out that the speed holds only if the object was far away; analyses of the original frames by the HoaxKiller project and others found the shape and motion of an insect a few metres from the lens.

title: The “mystery missile” off Los Angeles — an airliner’s contrail
place: Over the Pacific about 35 miles west of Los Angeles, north of Santa Catalina Island
explanation: A condensation trail from an airliner flying towards the camera, which made a horizontal trail look like a vertical column lit by the setting sun. The FAA’s radar replays found no fast unidentified target, the Pentagon said there was no evidence it was anything else, and NASA’s contrail specialists found the trail on GOES-11 satellite imagery as a horizontal streak. US Airways Flight 808 from Honolulu and UPS Flight 902 were named as candidates.
shape: A thick, glowing vapour trail apparently rising from the sea, with a bright head
witnesses: A KCBS news-helicopter crew; many people in the Los Angeles area
summary: At about 5:15 p.m. on November 8, 2010, a KCBS news helicopter filmed what looked like a missile climbing from the sea about 35 miles west of Los Angeles, a thick vapour trail glowing orange against the sunset with a bright point at its head. The footage ran on every network as the “mystery missile”, and for a day and a half nobody official could say what it was: the Pentagon said it was not a Defense Department launch, NORAD and Northern Command said it was no foreign military launch and no threat, the Navy said it was not theirs, and the FAA had approved no commercial launch. Contrail specialists and the analyst John Pike said at once that it was an aircraft contrail seen end-on, the head of the trail moving far too slowly for a rocket; the FAA’s radar replays found no fast unknown target, and on November 10 the Pentagon said there was “no evidence to suggest that this is anything else other than a condensation trail from an aircraft.” NASA researchers later found the trail on the GOES-11 weather-satellite image as a long horizontal streak. A few experts said they could not rule out a missile, but the incident is now a textbook example of foreshortened perspective.

title: The light over the Dome of the Rock (hoax)
place: Dome of the Rock, Temple Mount (Haram al-Sharif), Old City of Jerusalem
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: The videos were faked. They were posted anonymously; nobody else among the many people in and around the Old City reported the light; it casts no reflection on the gilded dome; one clip was filmed off a monitor screen; and the analyst Robert Sheaffer showed that the camera shake had been added with an edge-mirroring “motion tile” effect. Nobody has owned up, but no one who examined the clips found them genuine.
shape: A bright white light that descends, hovers over the dome, flashes and shoots straight up
witnesses: The anonymous uploaders of four videos; no independent witness
summary: In late January 2011 a YouTube video appeared showing a small bright light dropping slowly toward the Dome of the Rock some time after midnight on January 28, hovering just above the golden dome, flashing, and then shooting straight up out of sight. A second clip from another angle followed, then two more, posted under the challenge “Have fun debunking this one”. The videos went round the world, with commentators noting that the multiple viewpoints made them hard to dismiss. Within days investigators pointed to the anonymous sources, the lack of any other witness in one of the most watched places on Earth, the missing reflection on the dome and signs of editing, and the case became a standard example of a digitally inserted UFO.

title: Santiago — the silver spheres over the Paseo Bulnes
explanation: The objects were silver helium balloons released from the Paseo Bulnes by architecture students of the Universidad Mayor, one of four groups in a school competition; the installation was meant to block the view of La Moneda.
shape: Six bright silvery spheres
witnesses: Hundreds of people in the centre of Santiago
summary: On Friday, May 11, 2012, hundreds of people in the centre of Santiago stopped to watch a group of six bright, silvery spheres in the sky. Photographs and videos spread under the hashtag #OvnisEnStgo, and the sighting became a national talking point within hours. The same day it emerged that the spheres were silver helium balloons released from the Paseo Bulnes by students of the Universidad Mayor’s school of architecture, as an installation in a competition between four student groups intended to screen the view towards the La Moneda palace.

title: Ladakh lights — the “Chinese drones” that were planets
place: Thakung post, near Pangong Tso, eastern Ladakh, India
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: Astronomers of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, sent at the army’s request, identified the two brightest “objects” as Jupiter and Venus, made unusually bright by the altitude; their apparent motion was the sky turning. The defence minister told Parliament there was no conclusive proof of UFOs.
shape: Yellowish luminous spheres rising from the horizon on the Chinese side
witnesses: Indian Army and Indo-Tibetan Border Police troops
duration: August 2012 to February 2013; hours each night
summary: From August 2012, soldiers and border police on the Line of Actual Control in eastern Ladakh reported luminous objects rising over the Chinese side and staying up for hours. With Chinese drones a real concern, the army logged 329 sightings by February 2013 and counted 155 apparent violations of the border. At the army’s request, two astronomers from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics in Bengaluru travelled to Thakung, near Pangong Tso, and measured the objects with a theodolite: one was visible from about 6 p.m. to 5 a.m., the other from about 4 a.m., and they moved with the stars. They were Jupiter and Venus. A soldier’s note that one object rose about four minutes earlier every day, as a planet does, had already pointed the same way.

title: Chelyabinsk meteor — and the “UFO that shot it down”
place: Chelyabinsk Oblast, Russia; the air burst south of Chelyabinsk
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: A near-Earth asteroid about 20 m across entered at about 19 km/s at a shallow angle and exploded some 30 km up with the energy of roughly 400–500 kilotons of TNT, recorded by infrasound stations worldwide and by U.S. government sensors. Meteorites were collected across the strewn field, and a 654 kg fragment was raised from Lake Chebarkul in October 2013. Claims that videos showed a UFO destroying the meteor, and a newspaper survey in which many readers preferred a weapon test or a crashing alien ship, rest on nothing but the footage of the meteor itself.
shape: A fireball brighter than the Sun, leaving a long, twisted smoke trail
witnesses: Hundreds of thousands in Chelyabinsk Oblast and neighbouring regions; filmed by hundreds of dashboard and security cameras
duration: About 15 seconds of flight; the shock wave arrived one to three minutes later
summary: At 9:20 a.m. on February 15, 2013, a fireball brighter than the Sun crossed the morning sky of the southern Urals from the east and exploded south of Chelyabinsk, leaving a smoke trail tens of kilometres long. A minute or more later the shock wave blew in windows across the city: 1,491 people sought medical help, most cut by glass, and more than 7,000 buildings were damaged. Because Russian drivers routinely run dashboard cameras, the event was filmed from hundreds of angles, which let scientists reconstruct its path and orbit within days. Within hours, too, clips circulated claiming that a small object had flown into the meteor and shattered it, and the UFO commentator Gennady Belimov said a UFO had shot it down; a survey by the newspaper Noviye Izvestia found barely half its readers accepted the official account. The fragments in museum collections are ordinary chondrite.

title: Collahuasi mine — CEFAA’s “UFO” photographs
place: Collahuasi copper mine, 4,300 m up in the Tarapacá Andes
shape: A silver disc, estimated 5 to 10 m across
witnesses: Four technicians at the mine (anonymous); the photographs reached CEFAA through the chief engineer
summary: On a clear day in mid-April 2013, four technicians at the Collahuasi copper mine, high in the Andes of northern Chile, watched a silver disc hover silently for more than an hour at what they estimated as about 600 m, and one of them took photographs with a compact camera. They kept quiet until the mine’s chief engineer sent two pictures to CEFAA in February 2014. A CEFAA analyst at the meteorological office ruled out lenticular cloud, aircraft, drones, balloons and birds, found the object brighter than reflected sunlight would make it, and concluded it “can be qualified as a UFO”; the director, retired General Ricardo Bermúdez, released the study in July 2014 but said it was one analyst’s view and that the committee had to be cautious. The witnesses never answered CEFAA’s requests to talk, the originals and the order of the pictures were uncertain, and critics noted that a disc against blue sky gives no way to judge its size or distance. CEFAA filed the case as unexplained.

title: Aguadilla thermal video (DHS)
place: Rafael Hernández Airport, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: AARO assesses with high confidence the objects showed no anomalous speed or behaviour: a reconstruction of the sensor’s look angle shows two objects travelling near each other in a straight line at wind speed, never entering the water. Its case resolution assesses with moderate confidence that they were a pair of sky lanterns. Some independent analysts still dispute this.
shape: Small hot object; appears to enter and exit the sea
witnesses: U.S. Customs and Border Protection aircrew; tower controllers
summary: A Customs and Border Protection DHC-8 recorded a small, hot object crossing the airport and heading out over the ocean, where it appeared to plunge into the water and re-emerge. The leaked video became a staple of UAP analysis; AARO published a 3D reconstruction video in 2025.

title: Naga fireballs of the Mekong
place: The Mekong around Phon Phisai and Nong Khai, Thailand, and the Lao bank opposite
explanation: In 2002 a documentary on Thailand’s iTV filmed Lao soldiers on the far bank firing tracer rounds into the air during the festival, and the Thai biologist Jessada Denduangboripant, after studying footage, concluded the lights were flares fired from the other side. Neither explanation is accepted locally, and a Lao government inquiry in 2021, held during a COVID-19 curfew with police on the river, said it was “extremely unlikely” anyone could have fired unnoticed. The idea of phosphine or methane from the riverbed has no scientific support.
shape: Reddish-pink balls of light rising silently from the river to a few hundred metres
witnesses: Tens of thousands of festival visitors each year
duration: Seconds each; tens to thousands a night, on the night of Ok Phansa
summary: Every year on the night of Wan Ok Phansa, the full moon that ends the Buddhist Rains Retreat in October, crowds gather along a 250 km stretch of the Mekong centred on Phon Phisai to watch glowing reddish balls rise silently from the water, climb a few hundred metres and vanish. Local belief credits the phaya nak, the serpent said to live in the river; until the mid-1980s they were called ghost lights, and the Phayanak festival now draws tens of thousands of visitors. The photograph here was taken near Nong Khai on Ok Phansa night, 2013. Sceptics point to gunfire and flares from the Lao bank, which the crowds would not hear across the river; believers point out that the lights also appear over ponds and smaller rivers away from the border.

title: Chilean Navy helicopter FLIR video
place: Coast between San Antonio and Quinteros, Chile
explanation: Chile’s aerial-phenomena office (CEFAA) left the case open because it could not be certain of the object’s nature. Later analyses by sceptics proposed an aircraft’s contrail and exhaust seen by infrared as the likely cause.
shape: Flat, elongated object with two hot discharges
witnesses: Navy helicopter crew (pilot and camera operator)
summary: On November 11, 2014 a Chilean Navy helicopter on coastal patrol west of Santiago, at about 4,500 feet, picked up an unknown object on its high-definition infrared camera. The two-man crew also saw it with the naked eye for more than ten minutes. The captain described a flat, elongated object with two thermal discharges that did not line up with its direction of travel, and the video shows what looks like a chemical plume. The Navy’s aerial-phenomena office CEFAA examined it and later released the footage, saying it could not be sure what it was. Sceptics later said the images match the contrail of a distant aircraft.

title: USS Theodore Roosevelt — Gimbal & GoFast
place: Atlantic warning areas off Jacksonville, Florida
explanation: Both videos were officially released and remain "unidentified" per DoD. Analysts such as Mick West argue GoFast shows a slow object (e.g. a balloon) at ~13,000 ft that only looks fast and low because of parallax, and that Gimbal’s rotation is a glare artifact of the ATFLIR pod. AARO later published a case resolution for GoFast worked out from the sensor’s geometry and the winds aloft.
evidence: video | sensor-data | radar | pilot-witness | military-witness | official-document
shape: Rotating lozenge (Gimbal); small fast object (GoFast)
witnesses: VFA-11 aircrew; Lt. Ryan Graves’ squadron reported near-daily objects
duration: Seconds of video; months of sightings
summary: In 2014–2015 F/A-18F crews of the Roosevelt strike group reported frequent unknown objects on their upgraded APG-79 radars off the East Coast. Two ATFLIR clips — "Gimbal", with a crew member exclaiming about "a whole fleet of them", and "GoFast", a small object skimming over the ocean — were released by the Pentagon in April 2020.

title: The light over California — a Trident II test from USS Kentucky
place: The Navy’s Pacific Test Range off Southern California; seen from California, Nevada and Arizona
explanation: An unarmed Trident II (D5) ballistic missile fired by the submarine USS Kentucky during a scheduled test in the Pacific Test Range. The Navy confirmed it the same evening; its exhaust plume, lit by sunlight high above the darkened ground, produced the expanding “twilight phenomenon”.
shape: A bright light trailing a glowing, expanding cone of blue-white vapour
witnesses: Thousands of people from San Francisco to San Diego, Las Vegas and Phoenix
summary: Shortly after 6 p.m. on Saturday, November 7, 2015, a bright light rose over the Pacific west of Los Angeles and grew into a glowing, spreading cone of vapour that was seen from the Bay Area to San Diego and as far as Nevada and Arizona. Police and sheriff’s offices across Southern California were flooded with calls, and the videos spread across social media as a UFO, a meteor or a missile gone wrong. The Navy said that evening that its Strategic Systems Programs had carried out a scheduled test flight of an unarmed Trident II D5 missile from USS Kentucky in the Pacific Test Range; such launches are not announced in advance. The effect, sunlight catching the exhaust plume high above a darkened ground, is the same as the Iridium launch of 2017 and many Vandenberg twilight launches before it.

title: Fireball over the West — a Chinese rocket stage re-entering
explanation: The Joint Space Operations Center confirmed that the objects were the second stage of China’s Long March 7 rocket, launched on its first flight on June 25, 2016, re-entering the atmosphere and breaking up.
shape: A slow procession of bright fragments with glowing trails
witnesses: Thousands of people in California, Nevada, Utah, Idaho and Colorado
duration: More than 30 seconds in view from most places
summary: At about 9:36 p.m. on July 27, 2016, a slow procession of bright fragments with long trails crossed the sky over California, Nevada and Utah, seen from Los Angeles to Las Vegas and Salt Lake City and filmed by many people. It moved far more slowly than a meteor. Within hours the Joint Space Operations Center at Vandenberg confirmed that it had tracked the re-entry of the spent second stage of China’s new Long March 7 rocket, launched a month earlier, and later removed the object from the satellite catalogue as decayed. The astronomer Jonathan McDowell identified the stage from the tracking data. Like the Zond IV fragments of 1968, it is the kind of event that turns into a “formation of craft” in some witnesses’ descriptions.

title: Jeffreys Bay — a cargo crew’s green light
place: About 10 nautical miles off Jeffreys Bay, Eastern Cape
explanation: A green parachute flare was suspected first and ruled out because a flare cannot climb that high; the NSRI found no vessel or aircraft overdue or missing. Green is the usual colour of a bright meteor, but a meteor does not climb, which is what the crew described. The NSRI called the incident “a mystery”.
shape: A glowing green object
witnesses: The captain and first officer of a Boeing 737 freighter flying from Cape Town to Port Elizabeth
summary: At about 9:30 p.m. on December 12, 2016, the crew of a Boeing 737 cargo flight from Cape Town to Port Elizabeth, about 10 nautical miles off the coast at Jeffreys Bay, saw a glowing green object climb past the cockpit to the cloud layer some 1,000 feet above them, then turn and drop back past them toward the sea at high speed. Port Elizabeth air traffic control, fearing a vessel or aircraft in distress had fired a flare, asked the National Sea Rescue Institute to check; its Jeffreys Bay station watched overnight. The object was not seen again and no craft was overdue.

title: AARO’s “Southeast Asia Triangles” — fishing nets
place: A river in Southeast Asia (exact location withheld)
explanation: AARO, with intelligence and three science-and-technology partners, found “almost certainly” static, cone-shaped fishing nets on a river, each about 11 by 7 m, matched in other satellite images from 2017, 2022 and 2023 and in stock footage of the same river.
shape: Six dark triangles in a line
witnesses: An intelligence analyst reviewing satellite imagery
summary: A commercial satellite image taken at 07:35 UTC on August 30, 2017 showed six dark triangles in a staggered line, and an intelligence analyst flagged them as possibly anomalous and a risk to navigation. AARO reviewed the case in 2023. Its partners found a clearer image of the same place from February 2017 that showed the triangles as cone-shaped fishing nets anchored in a river, all about 11 by 7 metres; later images from late 2022 and early 2023 showed the same shapes with turbidity trailing downstream, proving they were in the water, and stock footage showed such nets on that river. AARO closed the case as fishing nets. Its report names only “Southeast Asia”; the image’s time stamps, 07:35Z and 14:05 local, match Myanmar’s clock (UTC+6:30), and the marker is placed there only approximately.

title: The Los Angeles “UFO” — SpaceX Iridium-4 launch
place: Vandenberg Air Force Base; seen across Southern California and as far as Arizona
explanation: A scheduled Falcon 9 launch carrying ten Iridium NEXT satellites from Vandenberg; the exhaust plume, lit by the Sun after sunset on the ground, made the glowing cloud. The Los Angeles Fire Department issued an advisory that the light came from the launch.
shape: A glowing, expanding jellyfish-like cloud with a bright point at its head
witnesses: Thousands across Southern California, Nevada and Arizona
summary: At 5:27 p.m. on December 22, 2017, twenty minutes after sunset, a Falcon 9 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg carrying ten Iridium NEXT satellites. High above the darkening ground the exhaust was still in sunlight, and the expanding plume, the staging and the fairing separation drew a luminous, jellyfish-like cloud seen from Los Angeles to Las Vegas and Phoenix. Phones and social media filled with pictures of a UFO; the Los Angeles Fire Department put out an advisory that the “mysterious light in the sky” was the launch, and Elon Musk posted the video as a “nuclear alien UFO from North Korea”. The launch had been announced in advance; twilight launches from Vandenberg have caused the same reports since.

title: Learjet and American 1095 over Arizona — “something just passed over us”
place: Over southern Arizona, east of the Sonoran Desert National Monument
explanation: An FAA spokesperson suggested a high-altitude balloon, which need not carry a transponder or tell air traffic control; the area sees regular research and weather balloons. The controller could not see anything on radar, and the pilots, who saw it pass above and in the opposite direction, did not sound convinced. No report of a military aircraft or drone in the area emerged.
shape: A bright, reflective object several thousand feet above the airliners
witnesses: The crew of a Phoenix Air Learjet 36 and of American Airlines Flight 1095, an Airbus A321; the Albuquerque Center controller
duration: About six minutes for both reports
summary: On the afternoon of February 24, 2018, a Learjet 36 flying east at about 37,000 ft over southern Arizona asked Albuquerque Center whether anything had just passed over it; the controller had nothing, and the pilot said something had. The controller asked American Airlines Flight 1095, an Airbus A321 following on the same route, to watch for traffic above it within the next 15 miles; a few minutes later its crew reported that something had passed over them, two or three thousand feet higher, going the other way, and, asked whether it was moving or hovering, said it was very bright or reflective. Someone on the frequency suggested a Google balloon, which the airline crew doubted, and someone else called it a UFO. The FAA released the recording to reporters in March; it said the controller could not see any other aircraft and suggested a high-altitude balloon. Nothing more was published.

title: Ireland — airline pilots report fast lights
explanation: One pilot suggested a meteor or an object in re-entry, and an astronomer at the Armagh Observatory said the lights were most likely meteors. Air traffic control saw nothing on radar and no military exercises were running, so nothing has been confirmed.
shape: Very bright lights moving at high speed
witnesses: Crews of a British Airways and a Virgin Atlantic flight, and others
summary: At about 6:47 on the morning of November 9, 2018 the pilot of a British Airways flight from Montreal to London radioed Shannon air traffic control to ask whether military exercises were under way. A “very bright light” had come up on the left of the aircraft and “rapidly veered to the north”, then disappeared at very high speed. The crew of a Virgin Atlantic flight reported two bright lights that banked to the right and climbed away at what the pilot called “astronomical” speed, “like Mach 2”. Controllers saw nothing on radar, and no military exercises were taking place. The Irish Aviation Authority said it would investigate by confidentially interviewing the pilots. More than one crew reported it, and the story was carried by news outlets around the world.

title: USS Omaha sphere & USS Russell "pyramids"
explanation: The Pentagon confirmed the leaked clips were taken by Navy personnel. Analysts attribute the "pyramids" to the triangular aperture of a night-vision lens (bokeh) on aircraft/stars, and the Omaha sphere to a distant aircraft or balloon.
shape: Spherical object descending into the sea; flashing pyramid shapes
witnesses: Crew of USS Omaha, USS Russell and other ships
summary: During July 2019, several Navy ships off Southern California reported drone-like objects around them at night. A CIC video from USS Omaha shows a sphere flying over the ocean and apparently descending into the water; night-vision footage from USS Russell shows blinking pyramid-shaped lights. Both leaked in 2021 and were confirmed as authentic Navy footage.

title: Colorado and Nebraska drone swarms
place: Phillips County and the plains of north-eastern Colorado
explanation: State and federal agencies found that most reports were planets, stars, aircraft and hobby drones, and the Colorado Department of Public Safety stood its effort down in January 2020. The large, grid-flying drones of the first reports were never tied to an operator.
shape: Drones with a wingspan of about 6 ft and blinking lights, in groups of six to ten, flying grid patterns
witnesses: Ranchers, residents and county sheriff’s deputies
summary: In December 2019, residents and deputies in north-eastern Colorado and western Nebraska began reporting drones with wingspans of about six feet flying in groups of six to ten, at 200 to 500 feet, in grid patterns across the plains, mostly between about 7 and 10 p.m.; one witness counted 19. County sheriffs asked the public for information, and more than 70 local, state and federal agencies met in Brush on January 6, 2020. The FAA said no drone company or test site had authorized flights there, and the Air Force, which had run counter-drone exercises at F. E. Warren AFB, would neither claim nor deny the drones. As the sightings spread, more and more turned out to be planets, stars and airliners, and the state ended its search later that month.

title: Sendai’s white balloon
explanation: A balloon. On February 14, 2023, after the Chinese balloon was shot down over the United States, Japan’s Ministry of Defense said that the balloons seen over its territory in November 2019, June 2020 and September 2021 were “strongly presumed” to be unmanned reconnaissance balloons flown by China; China rejected the claim.
shape: A large white sphere with crossed struts and propellers hanging beneath
witnesses: Residents of Sendai and Miyagi; the Sendai City Observatory photographed it
summary: On the morning of June 17, 2020, residents of northern Sendai began posting photographs of a large white sphere hanging almost motionless in the sky, with crossed struts and propellers beneath it. The Sendai office of the Japan Meteorological Agency said it looked like a weather balloon “but it’s not ours”, police sent a helicopter but could not identify it, Kyushu University denied it was theirs, and the government said only that it was aware of the object, which later drifted out over the Pacific. In February 2023, after the Chinese balloon crossed the United States, Japan’s Ministry of Defense re-examined the Sendai balloon and similar ones over Kagoshima in 2019 and Aomori in 2021, and concluded that they were strongly presumed to be Chinese unmanned reconnaissance balloons. It protested to Beijing, which said Japan had no proof.

title: American Airlines 2292 — “cruise-missile type of thing”
place: Northeastern New Mexico, at about 36,000 ft
explanation: No explanation has been given. The FAA said air traffic controllers saw no object on their radar. The Pentagon said the military was not conducting tests in the area that day, and the FBI said it was aware of the report.
shape: Long cylinder, “almost like a cruise missile”
witnesses: The crew of American Airlines Flight 2292
summary: On February 21, 2021, at about 12:29 p.m. local time, the crew of American Airlines Flight 2292, an Airbus A320 flying from Cincinnati to Phoenix at about 36,000 feet over the north-east corner of New Mexico, radioed: “Do you have any targets up here? We just had something go right over the top of us. I hate to say this, but it looked like a long cylindrical object that almost looked like a cruise missile type of thing, moving really fast right over the top of us.” The transmission was recorded by Steve Douglass, a radio listener. American Airlines at first denied that it was authentic, then confirmed that it was from Flight 2292 after talking to the crew. The FAA said controllers saw nothing on radar, and the Pentagon said it had no tests in the area.

title: Lights over Seattle and Portland — a Falcon 9 stage re-entering
place: Over western Oregon and Washington; debris in Grant County, Washington
explanation: The second stage of a SpaceX Falcon 9 that launched Starlink satellites on March 4, 2021, failed to make its de-orbit burn and re-entered uncontrolled about three weeks later. The National Weather Service in Seattle identified the lights the same night, and a pressure vessel from the stage was found on a farm in Grant County, Washington, and recovered by SpaceX.
shape: A cluster of bright fragments with glowing trails, moving slowly across the sky
witnesses: Thousands of people in western Oregon and Washington
summary: At about 9 p.m. on March 25, 2021, people from Portland to Seattle saw a slow cluster of bright lights with trails cross the sky, breaking apart as it went, and posted videos of what many took for a meteor shower or a formation of craft. The National Weather Service office in Seattle said that night that the lights were the remnants of a Falcon 9 second stage re-entering; the astronomer Jonathan McDowell confirmed that the stage, left in orbit after a Starlink launch on March 4 when its de-orbit burn failed, had come down at about 04:00 UTC on March 26. Days later a farmer in Grant County, in central Washington, reported to the sheriff an object that had left a four-inch dent in his field: a composite-overwrapped pressure vessel from the stage, which SpaceX identified and collected. It is one of the few re-entries where the identification, the tracking and a piece of the object all came together.

title: Three objects on a Western U.S. military range
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: AARO matched the three dots to commercial airliners far from the infrared sensor using flight and radar data.
shape: Three small dots on infrared
witnesses: Range sensor operators
summary: Shown by AARO at NASA’s UAP Independent Study Team public meeting (May 31, 2023) as an example of a resolved case: three unidentified infrared dots turned out to be three separate commercial aircraft at great distance.

title: Maldonado — the UFO videos that were a festival campaign
place: Parque del Jagüel, Punta del Este, Maldonado
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: The Uruguayan Air Force’s CRIDOVNI investigated and said the events “are not real”: the videos were part of a promotional campaign for the America Rockstars festival, including a staged television news flash.
shape: Not described; staged footage
witnesses: None independent; the footage was produced for an advertising campaign
summary: On August 12, 2021, videos circulated in Uruguay that appeared to show a UFO landing, U.S. aircraft and U.S. scientists at the Parque del Jagüel in Maldonado, with one clip presented as a breaking-news report by a well-known Subrayado journalist. The Uruguayan Air Force’s commission for UFO reports, CRIDOVNI, examined the material and announced the next day that, having investigated the evidence and analysed the possible events, they “are not real”. The clips turned out to be part of a promotional campaign for the America Rockstars music festival.

title: AC-130J “cold orbs” over the Gulf of Oman
explanation: AARO released the six clips in 2026 as unresolved. They are phone recordings of the gunship’s infrared display, not the sensor data itself, which limits what can be measured; the accompanying Intelligence Information Report describes “cold orbs” about four feet across.
shape: “Cold orbs”, approximately four feet in diameter
witnesses: The crew of a U.S. Special Operations Forces AC-130J gunship
summary: On September 8, 2021, the crew of a U.S. Special Operations AC-130J Ghostrider gunship over the Gulf of Oman tracked what an Intelligence Information Report (DOW-UAP-D101) calls “cold orbs” about four feet in diameter. U.S. Central Command sent AARO six short videos, recorded at the same time on a mobile phone pointed at the infrared sensor display. In most of them a small area of contrast stays in the centre of the sensor’s view; in two overlapping clips a larger and a smaller one cross the frame and come back. The Department of War released them as DOW-UAP-PR117 to PR122 in 2026, without a determination.

title: FBI files — orbs over one place in the north-eastern U.S.
