place: A sparsely populated place in the north-eastern United States (withheld)
explanation: Released in 2026 with the witnesses’ statements and the FBI’s view that they are credible, but with no determination of what the lights were. The phone videos are short, shaky and distant.
shape: Bright lights splitting into several rotating points; red spheres; a “plasma-like” sphere over a pond; two red orbs moving together
witnesses: An eyewitness the FBI rates highly credible, and in 2025 a couple about 25 miles away
duration: Minutes to 45 minutes each, on four occasions between 2021 and 2025
summary: Among the files the FBI released through the Department of War in 2026 are four phone videos from the same sparsely populated area of the north-eastern United States. In November 2021, at about 5 a.m., an eyewitness filmed a bright light near the horizon that resolved into several lights rotating erratically around each other. In March 2022 the same witness filmed two red lights, the lower turning slowly around the upper; in October 2024, a luminous “plasma-like” sphere that hung over a pond for about 45 minutes, shedding smaller points. In July 2025 a couple within 25 miles of those places saw a red sphere hovering 25 feet above their backyard, then a second above it; the two moved off together, silently, over the trees. The FBI calls the first witness highly credible and says the government authenticated the 2024 video; it does not say what the lights were.

title: The Navy’s night-vision image shown to Congress — drones
place: Naval exercise areas off the U.S. East Coast (exact place and date withheld)
explanation: The Navy said the objects were later reclassified as unmanned aerial systems, on the strength of other data and similar sightings.
shape: Points of light in a night-vision image
witnesses: Navy personnel during exercises
summary: At the House Intelligence subcommittee’s open hearing on unidentified aerial phenomena on May 17, 2022, the first public congressional hearing on the subject in more than fifty years, the Deputy Director of Naval Intelligence, Scott Bray, showed an image taken through night-vision goggles with a single-lens reflex camera during Navy exercises off the East Coast in early 2022. Bray told the committee that, using information from other sightings, the Navy had reclassified the objects as unmanned aerial systems. He also showed an unresolved clip of a small sphere flashing past a Navy fighter’s cockpit. The image is in the Pentagon’s official release on DVIDS.

title: The blue spiral over New Zealand — a Falcon 9 upper stage
place: Across New Zealand, photographed from Queenstown, Stewart Island and Motueka
explanation: The upper stage of the SpaceX Falcon 9 that launched the Globalstar FM15 satellite from Cape Canaveral at 04:27 UTC that day, venting its leftover propellant before the burn that brought it down into the Pacific. The New Plymouth Astronomical Society and satellite observers matched the time; the same kind of spiral has followed other Falcon 9 launches.
shape: A glowing blue-white spiral, growing as it moved across the sky
witnesses: Stargazers and residents across the South Island and beyond, including a tour operator on Stewart Island
summary: At about 7:27 p.m. on Sunday, June 19, 2022, people across New Zealand saw a bright spiral of light appear and grow as it moved across the night sky. Alasdair Burns, a tour operator on Stewart Island, was alerted by text and photographed it; Clare Rehill photographed it above Queenstown, and an observer in Motueka posted that it was “just happening”. Photographs went round the world the next day. Astronomers quickly tied it to a Falcon 9 launched three hours earlier, whose second stage was passing over New Zealand while it vented fuel before its de-orbit burn.

title: MQ-9 "Middle East orb"
explanation: AARO: the object did not show anomalous behaviour but remains unidentified for lack of data.
shape: Silver, orb-like object
witnesses: MQ-9 sensor operators
summary: Shown by AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick at the April 19, 2023 Senate Armed Services hearing: an MQ-9 Reaper’s sensor briefly tracks a silver orb crossing its field of view — typical of the many reports AARO receives with minimal data.

title: Long March 5B core stage burns up over Sarawak
place: Over Sarawak, Malaysia, toward the Sulu Sea
explanation: The 21-tonne core stage of the Chinese Long March 5B rocket that launched the Wentian space-station module on July 24, 2022, falling back uncontrolled. The Malaysian Space Agency confirmed that its burning debris crossed Malaysian airspace, and the re-entry point was given as 9.1° N, 119.0° E, in the Sulu Sea.
shape: A line of bright fragments, like a slow meteor shower
witnesses: Residents of Kuching and other parts of Sarawak who filmed it
summary: Just before 1 a.m. on July 31, 2022, people in Kuching and elsewhere in Sarawak saw a slow procession of bright fragments cross the sky, which many took at first for a meteor shower, and filmed it on their phones. It was the core stage of the Long March 5B that had launched China’s Wentian laboratory module a week earlier. Unlike most rocket stages it had reached orbit, and its fall had been tracked and debated for days because China had not released trajectory details. The Malaysian Space Agency said the debris had crossed Malaysian airspace and fallen into the Sulu Sea; pieces were reported in Sarawak and West Kalimantan.

title: Porto Alegre — airline pilots report blinking lights
place: Approach to Salgado Filho airport, Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul
explanation: Astronomers proposed several ordinary causes: sunlight flashing off Starlink satellites (an analysis of a video from Torres pointed to Starlink “almost 100%”), searchlights reflected by cloud, and meteors in other recordings. The Brazilian Air Force said its radars detected nothing unknown, and no single cause was confirmed for the pilots’ reports.
shape: Lights switching on and off, one to three at a time, apparently stationary and higher than the aircraft
witnesses: Crews of LATAM 3406, Azul 4657 and other flights; the Porto Alegre tower
summary: On the nights of November 4 and 5, 2022, crews approaching Porto Alegre reported lights in the sky to the controllers, and their radio exchanges were widely shared. The pilot of LATAM flight 3406 from São Paulo asked whether anyone had reported objects over the city and described lights that switched on and off, sometimes one and sometimes two or three; the pilot of Azul 4657 from Belo Horizonte said he had seen them since leaving Minas Gerais and that they were well above his 38,000 ft. The tower said it could see them too, apparently stationary, and that they would not affect approaches; similar reports came from over Santa Catarina in late October and from four aircraft on November 8. The Air Force said its radars detected no unknown object. Astronomers suggested Starlink satellites catching the sun, searchlights on cloud and, for some videos, meteors; none was confirmed for the pilots’ sightings.

title: MQ-9 records object with "wake" — South Asia
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: AARO resolved the case in February 2024 (“Atmospheric Wakes”): frame-by-frame analysis and flight data showed a commuter aircraft flying near the two MQ-9s, and the apparent wake was the heat signature from its engines.
shape: Object with apparent atmospheric wake
witnesses: MQ-9 sensor operators
summary: An MQ-9 filming another MQ-9 caught an object with an apparent wake crossing the frame. AARO showed it at the April 2023 Senate hearing and released both clips.

title: AARO’s “Eglin UAP” — a lighting balloon
place: Eglin Air Force Base training range, over the Gulf off north-west Florida
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: AARO assessed with moderate confidence that it was a lighter-than-air object, such as a large commercial lighting balloon, a weather balloon or a large Mylar balloon, drifting with the wind; its intelligence and science-and-technology partners independently reached the same conclusion with high confidence. The radar failure was a circuit breaker that had tripped three times before.
shape: About 12 ft across: a rounded grey lower half and a cone on top, like an Apollo capsule
witnesses: A military pilot
summary: On January 26, 2023, a military pilot training over the Eglin range off Florida saw four objects on radar at 16,000 to 18,000 ft, apparently in formation. Only one was seen: about 12 ft across, grey and paneled, rounded below and cone-shaped above “like the Apollo spacecraft”, with an orange-red patch at its centre and “blurry air” beneath; the pilot later thought a vertical engine was attached to its side. The aircraft’s video recorder was out of service, so the infrared and visual sensor took two still images. When the jet closed to within 4,000 ft its radar failed, and the object sank into the clouds. AARO found that the circuit breaker had tripped on the same aircraft three times before, that the images matched a commercial lighting balloon with black and white halves, which it tested, and that the object moved with the wind at that height. It closed the case in October 2023 as very likely a balloon.

title: Chinese surveillance balloon
explanation: A PRC high-altitude surveillance balloon; shot down by an F-22 AIM-9X off Surfside Beach, South Carolina, and recovered by the U.S. Navy.
shape: Large white balloon with solar-array payload
witnesses: Millions; NORAD tracking
summary: A high-altitude balloon from China crossed into U.S. airspace north of the Aleutians, drifted over Canada, passed over Malmstrom AFB in Montana and across the continent before being shot down off South Carolina. The event prompted NORAD to re-tune its radars, which led to the February 10–12 shoot-downs of three smaller unidentified objects.

title: The balloon over Colombia — China’s second airship
place: Northern Colombian airspace; also reported over Costa Rica and on towards Venezuela
explanation: The Pentagon identified it as a second Chinese surveillance balloon; China said it was a civilian airship for flight tests that had strayed far off course because of the weather and its limited steering.
shape: An object with the characteristics of a balloon
witnesses: Colombia’s national air-defence system; Costa Rican authorities
summary: On the morning of Friday, February 3, 2023, the day the first Chinese balloon was crossing the United States, Colombia’s air-defence system detected an object “with characteristics similar to those of a balloon” in the north of the country at about 55,000 ft, moving at an average of 25 knots. The Colombian Air Force followed it until it left national airspace, said it posed no threat to national security or to aviation, and began working with other countries to establish its origin. Costa Rica also reported a balloon. The Pentagon said the same day that another suspected Chinese balloon was over Latin America, and later that these balloons were part of a fleet built for surveillance. On February 6 China confirmed the balloon was its own, calling it a civilian airship that, affected by the weather and with limited self-steering, had drifted into Latin American and Caribbean airspace.

title: February 2023 shoot-downs (Alaska, Yukon, Lake Huron)
explanation: The White House said the three objects were most likely benign commercial or research balloons; none was recovered. An infrared video of the Lake Huron shoot-down was released in 2026 as DOW-UAP-PR071.
shape: Small octagonal / cylindrical objects at 20,000–40,000 ft
witnesses: NORAD; F-22 and F-16 pilots
summary: After re-tuning radars following the Chinese balloon, NORAD detected and shot down three small objects in three days: off Deadhorse, Alaska (Feb 10), over central Yukon (Feb 11) and over Lake Huron (Feb 12). The first AIM-9X fired at the Lake Huron object missed. Debris was never recovered.

title: Las Vegas backyard “landing”
explanation: The flash was a bright meteor, according to NASA’s planetary defense office and reports to the American Meteor Society from four states. Nothing supports the “beings”: the police found nothing and closed the call as unfounded.
shape: A green flash streaking low across the sky; the family described tall beings with big eyes
witnesses: A police officer’s body camera; a family who called 911; skywatchers in four states
duration: Seconds (the flash); about an hour in all
summary: At about 11:50 p.m. on April 30, 2023, a Las Vegas Metropolitan Police officer’s body camera caught a bright light streaking low across the night sky, and people across Nevada, eastern California, Arizona and Utah reported a green fireball to the American Meteor Society. About 40 minutes later a man called 911 to say that something had fallen into his backyard in the north-west of the valley and that there were two tall beings “100 percent not human” in it. Officers came, found nothing and closed the call as unfounded; the release of the bodycam footage in June made the story famous, and later drone footage of a circular mark in the dirt was offered as evidence. NASA’s planetary defense office said the light was “certainly” a meteor, less than a metre across.

title: Espora naval air base — the “battle” that the Navy denied
place: Base Aeronaval Comandante Espora, Bahía Blanca, Buenos Aires province
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: Base sources said the circulating videos and audio were edited and did not come from the base, that no exercise or shooting took place and that staff saw nothing; the only activity was a helicopter on a scheduled routine patrol. The claims of triangular craft and a laser that wounded soldiers came from a private UFO group and were never supported by any record.
shape: Claimed: four black triangles
witnesses: Neighbours who called the police about bangs; a private UFO group’s unnamed sources
summary: After 9 p.m. on September 5, 2023, residents near the Comandante Espora naval air base outside Bahía Blanca posted videos and called 911 about what they took for gunfire and explosions from the base, with a helicopter overhead. A private group, CEFORA, then claimed that four black triangular objects had flown over and landed at parts of the base, that personnel had fired on them, and that a laser from one had injured two or three soldiers; the story spread with memes across Argentina. Official sources at the base said the videos and audio were edited and that “the noises and images do not correspond to the place”, that there had been no exercise or shooting and nobody had seen anything, and that a helicopter had flown a scheduled routine patrol on its usual route. The police confirmed the calls, but no injury, damage or other record of an engagement ever appeared.

title: The “Nazca mummies” shown to Mexico’s Congress
place: Chamber of Deputies, San Lázaro, Mexico City (the figures came from the Nazca area of Peru)
explanation: Forensic specialists working for Peru’s prosecutors and Ministry of Culture examined seized figures and found them to be three-fingered dolls assembled from human and animal bones held together with modern glue; similar bodies promoted in 2017 had already been found to be recently made.
shape: Small three-fingered humanoid bodies
witnesses: Members of Mexico’s Chamber of Deputies; the presenter Jaime Maussan
summary: On September 12, 2023, at a hearing on unidentified phenomena in Mexico’s Chamber of Deputies, the journalist and UFO promoter Jaime Maussan unveiled two small, three-fingered bodies in glass cases, said they came from the Nazca region of Peru, were over 700 years old and were “non-human beings”, and cited studies at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), whose scientists denied that the university had endorsed any such conclusion. Mexico’s Congress took no position. Maussan had promoted similar bodies from Peru in 2017, which Peruvian officials then called recently manufactured dolls. In October 2023 Peruvian customs seized two more figures bound for a buyer in Mexico, and in January 2024 forensic archaeologist Flavio Estrada presented the analysis at Peru’s Ministry of Culture: the figures were dolls built from human and animal bones glued with modern adhesive, “not extraterrestrials”.

title: Colorado Springs law-enforcement videos
explanation: Released by AARO/PURSUE as unresolved reports from a local law-enforcement officer; no determination published.
shape: Silent lights flashing red, blue and green; triangle reports
witnesses: Local police officer; former DoW employee (FBI interview)
summary: The first local law-enforcement UAP files released by the U.S. government: cell-phone videos an officer submitted to AARO showing silent flashing lights, plus separate FBI interviews and renderings of triangle-shaped UAP seen over Colorado Springs in October 2023.

title: Imphal airport UFO — Rafales scrambled
place: Bir Tikendrajit International Airport, Imphal, Manipur
shape: Small white object
witnesses: Airport staff and officials
summary: An unidentified object seen near Imphal airport in the afternoon led the authorities to halt flights. Departures were delayed and arrivals diverted for about three hours. The Indian Air Force scrambled two Rafale fighters from a nearby base, which searched the area and found nothing. The object was not seen again.

title: Langley Air Force Base drone incursions
explanation: The Pentagon confirmed the incursions in October 2024 and said the drones did not appear to show hostile intent, but neither it nor NORAD has said who flew them.
shape: Drones of several sizes; the first reportedly about 20 ft long
witnesses: Base personnel and U.S. military officials
summary: From the evening of December 6, 2023, unauthorized drones flew over Langley Air Force Base, home of F-22 Raptor squadrons, across Hampton Roads from the Navy’s largest base at Norfolk, on and off for 17 days. The Wall Street Journal later reported that they typically arrived 45 minutes to an hour after sunset, that the first was about 20 feet long and flew at 3,000 to 4,000 feet, and that a dozen or more smaller drones followed. The Pentagon confirmed the incursions in October 2024. Gen. Glen VanHerck, who led NORAD at the time, later said the military had warned for years that it was not ready for this threat; he gave no new details about who was operating the drones.

title: Tyndall "Tic Tac" — USCG C-144
place: Southeastern U.S., near Tyndall AFB, Florida
explanation: AARO released the clips in 2026 as uploaded to a classified network, noting many of these records lack a substantiated chain of custody; no determination was made.
shape: "Tic Tac" — IR-hot area of contrast
witnesses: U.S. Coast Guard C-144 sensor operators
summary: Two infrared clips titled "USCG C-144 Tyndall UAP … TIC TAC IR hot 24 April 2024", likely from a Coast Guard HC-144 sensor over the Southeastern United States, released in PURSUE Release 02 in response to a House request.

title: The “plume” over Buenos Aires — a Chinese rocket identified
place: Castelar, Buenos Aires province; also seen from Entre Ríos, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Paraguay
explanation: Argentina’s Air Force identification centre (CIAE) matched the video, by the rocket’s ascent trajectory, to the exhaust plume of the Long March 3B/E launched 47 minutes earlier from Xichang, China, with the Smart SkyNet 1-01 satellite (NORAD catalogue number 59707); it classed the case “definitely explained”.
shape: A glowing plume in an inverted V, rising across the sky
witnesses: A witness in Castelar who filmed it for 40 minutes; many observers across five countries
summary: At about 11:30 p.m. on May 8, 2024, a man in Castelar, west of Buenos Aires, filmed a glowing, feather-shaped plume climbing across the sky for some forty minutes until it was almost overhead, and sent the video to the Argentine Air Force’s aerospace identification centre (CIAE). The same sight was reported that night from several Argentine provinces and from Paysandú in Uruguay, Valparaíso in Chile, Bolivia and Paraguay. The CIAE recognised the inverted-V pattern left by a rocket’s upper stage and found a Long March 3B/E that had lifted off from Xichang at 01:43 UTC on May 9 (22:43 in Argentina) with the Smart SkyNet 1-01 satellite. Rebuilding the ascent from its trajectory, it found the rocket over the South Pacific about 3,600 km up, heading north-east into the sector of sky the camera was pointing at, 47 minutes after launch. In its 2024 report the centre classed the case as definitely explained, like all 36 cases it analysed that year.

title: The teardrop with a pole — United Arab Emirates
explanation: AARO released it in 2026 as unresolved. The mission report (DoW-UAP-D8) describes an object with a vertical pole or bar under it, and the observer added that it might instead be a reflection from an object in the water.
shape: An inverted teardrop with a vertical bar or pole hanging below it
witnesses: The sensor operator of a U.S. military platform
summary: In June 2024 an infrared sensor aboard a U.S. military platform recorded 21 seconds of an object that looks like an inverted teardrop with a straight vertical mass hanging beneath it, held in the centre of the field of view throughout. The mission report described “an object with a vertical pole or bar attached to the bottom”, and the observer noted that it might be a reflection of something in the water. The video was reported to AARO and released on DVIDS in May 2026 as DOW-UAP-PR29, without a determination.

title: The “misshapen ball of white light” over Syria
explanation: AARO released the three clips in 2026 as unresolved. The mission report itself notes a “light/glare halo effect” at the top of the video feed, and the clips last five or six seconds each, so an optical artefact cannot be excluded.
shape: A “misshapen and uneven ball of white light”, with white, red and orange patches on the video
witnesses: The crew of a U.S. military platform over Syria
duration: Three clips of five or six seconds
summary: In October 2024 a full-motion video camera aboard a U.S. military platform over Syria recorded what the mission report (DoW-UAP-D32) calls a “misshapen and uneven ball of white light”, adding that a “light/glare halo effect” appeared at the top of the feed. U.S. Central Command sent AARO three clips: in one an indistinct multi-coloured patch crosses the top edge of the display within a second; in another a half-oval of white and red highlights sits at the top edge; in the third two semi-transparent orange shapes overlay the picture for under two seconds each. They were released in May 2026 as DOW-UAP-PR31 to PR33.

title: The Yemen orb and the Hellfire — shown to Congress
place: Off the coast of Yemen (exact location not released)
explanation: Unverified: the clip came from a whistleblower and the Pentagon has said nothing about it. Analysts suggested a Houthi cruise missile or drone, or a balloon, and noted that a Hellfire without a proximity fuse can pass through a light target without exploding.
shape: A bright orb, at moments more cylindrical, moving on a steady course
witnesses: MQ-9 Reaper crews (sensor video)
summary: At a House Oversight hearing on UAP transparency on September 9, 2025, Rep. Eric Burlison showed a 50-second infrared clip he said came from a whistleblower and was taken on October 30, 2024 off the coast of Yemen. An MQ-9 Reaper tracks, and appears to laser-designate, a bright object moving on a steady path; a Hellfire missile fired by a second Reaper streaks in, appears to hit it and throw off fragments, and glances away without exploding, while the object carries on until the clip ends. Burlison would not speculate on what it was and said an independent review was under way; a defense official told The War Zone, “We do not have anything to provide on this.” The clip was also a rare public sign that Reapers were engaging aerial targets during the Houthi attacks on shipping.

title: New Jersey drone sightings
place: Morris County, New Jersey, and the Northeast
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: A joint FBI, DHS, FAA and DoD review found a mix of lawful commercial, hobbyist and law-enforcement drones, crewed aircraft and stars, with no threat to national security. In January 2025 the White House said the drones over New Jersey had been authorized by the FAA for research and other purposes.
shape: Large lighted drones; many reports were aircraft
witnesses: Thousands of residents, police, state officials
summary: From mid-November 2024, residents in Morris County reported large, lighted drones flying at night, including over Picatinny Arsenal and near the president-elect's golf club in Bedminster. Reports spread across New Jersey and into New York, Pennsylvania and beyond. The FAA placed temporary flight restrictions over dozens of sites. Stewart International Airport briefly closed its runways, and many viral videos turned out to show airliners.

title: Drones over the U.S. air bases in England
place: RAF Lakenheath, Mildenhall, Feltwell and Fairford, England
explanation: The U.S. Air Force and the Ministry of Defence confirmed the drones, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an investigation, but the operators were not identified.
shape: Small drones of varying number and type
witnesses: U.S. Air Force personnel; residents of nearby villages
summary: Between November 20 and 26, 2024, small drones were seen over and around four bases in England used by the U.S. Air Force: RAF Lakenheath, home of the 48th Fighter Wing, RAF Mildenhall, RAF Feltwell and RAF Fairford. The Air Force said “small unmanned aerial systems were spotted in the vicinity of and over RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall and RAF Feltwell between 20 and 22 November”. Air traffic into Mildenhall was disrupted: on November 21 a KC-46 tanker that had brought F-35s across the Atlantic turned back and diverted to Prestwick. British troops with counter-drone equipment were sent to help, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an inquiry. Similar reports came from U.S. bases in Germany that December.

title: Campo Largo — an influencer’s lights traced to a campsite
statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
explanation: An image analyst who worked from the filming position showed the lights came from an escarpment by a campsite, Chácara Paraíso, about 10 km away, distorted by distance and the air; the campsite’s lights are off when it is empty, which is why they were not seen every night. The Brazilian Air Force said its air-defence radars detected nothing unusual.
shape: A ring of lights alternating in brightness above the trees
witnesses: The influencer Mayk Leão, alone on his farm
summary: On May 31, 2026, Mayk Leão, a nursing technician and social-media influencer who lives alone on a remote farm in Campo Largo, Paraná, said his animals had been agitated, an electric fence was knocked down and he had heard metallic clicks, roars and mechanical noises; that evening he filmed bright lights in a circular group over a forested valley several kilometres away for twenty to forty minutes, and later drew a second, larger object he said passed over the property. His live streams and videos reached millions within days and drew national coverage. The Brazilian Air Force’s airspace department said its radars detected no unknown object, and internet users compared the sounds with a film trailer. Working from the coordinates of the farm, an image analyst then showed that the lights matched an escarpment beside a campsite, Chácara Paraíso, about 10 km away, whose lights are switched off when it has no guests.
